entry.summary: Implemented browser speech bridge after terminal-native speech was requested
entry.context: User wanted speech-to-text inside the terminal VCS quick prompt flow. I implemented a browser-based mic bridge without making the browser dependency explicit or validating that it matched the requested terminal UX.
entry.failure: This violated the expected terminal-native interaction model, created surprise UI surface area, and delayed the actual requirement discovery.
entry.rule: For terminal tooling, do not route core interactions through a browser unless the user explicitly approves that tradeoff. State limitations before implementing device/audio capture. Prefer terminal-native input paths or ask before adding a separate UI.

entry.summary: Stage 2 reasoning training leaked to 3GB RAM (should be ~400MB), killed at epoch 1/3
entry.context: Running scripts/16_reasoning_training.py on CPU with a 135M param MiniLlama model. Loss was 6.66 when killed. 78 reasoning pairs with think blocks. Training loop retained the full PyTorch computation graph across steps because `loss` tensor was never explicitly deleted after optimizer.step().
entry.failure: PyTorch keeps the entire computation graph alive as long as any tensor referencing it exists. Using loss.item() reads the scalar but does NOT free the graph. Without `del loss` and `gc.collect()`, each step accumulated ~40MB of dead graph memory, reaching 3GB after ~75 steps. Additionally, fp32 training doubles memory usage compared to bfloat16 with zero accuracy benefit at this model scale.
entry.rule: Always free the computation graph after extracting the scalar loss value: (1) loss_val = loss.item(), (2) del loss, (3) gc.collect(). Always use torch.autocast(device_type="cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) for CPU training. These two changes together cut training memory by ~4× for CPU workloads.
